crates.name: bboxy450-harness
crates.scope: Finite two-turn/two-tool lifecycle; birth fencing A-B-A, unattended approval, FIFO control, bounded replay/lag/reset and Yarn arbitration. HTTP/TCP bytes, filesystem/process effects, wall-clock deadlines, secrecy and terminal bytes are witnessed by implementation tests; no arbitrary Rust refinement claim.
implementation_only: Store writer lease (d20261103136541): one private non-Clone guard spans successful nonblocking acquisition, opening job/error/abandoned output, handoff and Store destruction. HarnessStoreWriterLease separately models old/replacement ownership, one inherited/fsync descriptor and successful/failed release with reachable missing/premature/stale controls. src/store.rs lease_tests and process.rs native pre-exec witness cover actual exclusion, checked/Drop errors, job abandonment, clone lifetime and replacement preservation; existing store_recovery/store_fork/ir_v1_corpus suites retain actual byte and fork custody. Supported successful kernel unlock is assumed for positive release; exceptional failure remains unavailable/best-effort, not certified release. General unsafe fork duplicating a Rust Store owner, arbitrary filesystem/kernel behavior and universal scheduling are not proved. Existing fork and process families stay unchanged.

Process spawn admission (d20261103136528): HarnessProcessSpawnAdmission abstracts one queued request, local cancellation/drop/deadline, one exclusive worker/result/caller/retirement owner and one reservation through reap. Reachable late-queue and lost-owner controls are paired; tests/formal_nonvacuity.rs covers real queue/drop/handoff/return-before-cleanup states. src/process.rs spawn_admission_tests and tests/cancel_process.rs use held existing permits, private barriers/children and actual reap/environment witnesses; tests/dream_pipeline.rs retains the D0/owned-spawn CPU regression. Command bytes, actual CPU/OS scheduling, Tokio signals, cryptography and arbitrary timings remain implementation-only. API cancellation/return is not joined producer admission cleanup or a constructive seal; WP9 must independently observe/join it. The existing ProcessLifecycle family is unchanged and retains group/member/reap fencing.

D1 prompt and JSON parsing, NFC EntryId/record bytes, exact source/Event/Task pins, independent trust, deny/redaction, 60k-byte conservative input/32KiB output bounds, <=3 candidates, Usage and private-HOME process behavior are implementation witnesses in tests/dream_pipeline.rs, not facts proved by lifecycle/provider quotients. D1 accepts the caller-owned Store and never instantiates tools, retries, a scheduler, adoption or a second writer. Its standalone scripted output remains semantic-audit UNPROVEN without WP4/WP9 final receipts; real provider/profile/quota scheduling and full receipt/seal integration are caller responsibilities.

Private provenance record memoization uses safe hashbrown0.17.1 HashTable of existing Arc<ResolvedRecord>, borrowed full-pin hashing/equality and production std RandomState. dream::resolve private units cover complete fields/Option identity under forced collisions, resizing/rehash, duplicate Arc retention, clear and independent random seeds with identical canonical observable records. tests/dream_identity.rs drives actual read-only Resolver Arc reuse, exact alias/None/Some identities, rejected pins, missing-file retry and policy authorization/revocation invalidation. No lock, retry, persistence or lifecycle contract changes. The immutable private index is abstracted by existing models; their bounds do not prove hashbrown/allocator/Hasher memory safety, hash quality, allocation counts or benchmark timings. The ignored release cache kernel compares old serde-JSON+BTreeMap hits with the actual helper; serialized-key payload lengths are separate from process memory and no end-to-end speed claim or CI timing gate is made.

WP4 Adoption ownership is checked for every selected-log fact against its qualifying publication/session/full fields and local contiguous suffix; actual API/CLI foreign-session, seven altered-field/duplicate cases and local/cross-log ordinal controls exercise this pure boundary. Existing finite DreamSink identities remain opaque and do not prove Rust session/digest/seq binding. WP4 reported Recall/sink-line controls distinguish accepted successful publication from a valid skipped receipt; skips retain diagnostics but never authorize insertion or generated-line provenance. WP4 source/API/process coverage: exact NFC identity, V/T external trust/2 policy, noncircular source-build-gate-report-task approval, canonical Receipt/R1-R4/E, retained cut/source prefixes, deterministic selection/rendering/adoption/header/outer-seal bindings and finite read-only why/graph/audit. HarnessDreamSeal has recording/frozen/sealed/closed, zero/one child, observed/enforced coverage and one in-flight effect; no arbitrary IO fairness or Rust/hash/syscall proof. Before the owner token was introduced, nonvacuity checked the good graph and both actual late-write/live-child controls. dream_seal has constructive no-self-hash/prefix/suffix/child/cut/field controls and a real private delayed-child/ABA observer; dream_trust uses actual private OpenPGP Git gates/reports and executable identity; dream_audit_broken materializes complete trusted retained publication/run/idempotent/stale-exposure fixtures and executes actual read-only CLI queries, alongside named P1-P9 negatives. Producer effect completeness and real filesystem confinement/durability are approved executable/W obligations, not inferred from child rows, matching bytes or quotient membership. No live policy/bootstrap or producer approval is installed. Native loader/consolidation state is excluded; missing Grok native scope configuration is unproven. WP8/9 retain product observer/gate and final combined source/model/process evidence responsibilities.

Receipt IR carrier is a passive additive variant and a member of the existing fork referenced-blob collection, with no new lifecycle/arbitration/model semantics. tests/protocol_golden.rs and tests/ir_v1_corpus.rs witness receipt_kind, optional/defaulted fields, recursive Unknown writer rejection, unchanged old Adoption validity, real session receipt blobs, exact envelope bytes over Store/fork/Unix/headless, and missing/corrupt blob refusal. Receipt body interpretation, semantic audit, causal cuts, trust policy and producer approval are not proved by the fork quotient and remain with WP4.

WP3 D0 pin-set cache: HarnessDreamD0 separates nonblocking claim acquisition/busy skip, read, union, atomic publication, caller return and crash release; it uses two workers/two shards/two opaque pins, one crash/one replay and no IO fairness. tests/dream_replay.rs drives the actual cache API, a private claim-owning Rust child killed/reaped by its test parent, independent shards, duplicate union, detached close while all four existing blocking permits are occupied, real signed Git task enumeration and a ref moved between enumeration/pinned reads. Expensive walks/parsing/union/persistence use the existing permit-backed blocking helper with thread assertions. Actual future polls enforce/report the one-millisecond thread CPU cap, with an inline CPU broken control. Task joins in src/dream/join.rs do not implement WP4 lifecycle projection; source presence is not that model's conformance. Native custody now stages ordinary deterministic imported IR in the selected sessions root, with snapshot caps of 16MiB/10000 records and a 128MiB custody-file validation cap. HarnessDreamNativeCustody checks staged/complete publication separately, with a premature-pin control. tests/dream_replay.rs checks Claude/Codex and independent-root bytes/blobs, exact pins, repeat/rebuild/races, changing/malformed input, private-stage crash/complete survivor reuse, and conflicting logs/blobs without clobber. Native EOF remains explicitly unproven process completion. Flock/kernel crash release, rename/fsync, actual byte/identity/digest resolution, Git/percentile semantics, arbitrary OS/filesystem scheduling and universal CPU/wall-clock behavior remain implementation-only; finite model parity is not a Rust/kernel proof. WP9 retains final combined mappings.

WP2 VCS metadata: src/vcs.rs reuses process::capture_stdout and its existing owned-process reservation, timeout, kill/drain/reap contracts; no new process owner, retry queue or lifecycle is introduced. tests/dream_vcs.rs exercises actual Git repo/no-origin/dirty/credential URL data, engine+ACP headers (including inherited Git Trace2 environment-secret controls), missing/failing Git, and deadline termination/reaping of a stalled Git group. tests/import_native.rs checks Claude branch-only/Codex partial/full native availability, unguessed absent fields, preserved unknown native Git fields and credential-free raw/ext projection; tests/cli_headless.rs checks no-repo metadata and byte-identical closed replay without invoking Git. A three-second shared query budget, 16KiB stdout cap and inherited bounded process cleanup constrain work; canonicalization runs on the existing permit-backed blocking helper. Git parsing, changing-checkout snapshot consistency (observations are not an atomic Git transaction), URL semantics, syscall scheduling, bytes, actual wall-clock bounds and external Git configuration behavior remain implementation-only; the inherited finite process models are not a Rust/Git refinement proof. Live-watch/reproject header promotion remains outside this WP2 scope; unknown native data is retained.

The current WP4 pure validator/projection APIs are mapped separately; WP6 D1 now uses the existing single Store/provider contracts with actual strict prompt/parse, request-capture, private-HOME CLI and zero-tool-execution witnesses in tests/dream_pipeline.rs. Trial/sink product implementation remains pending WP7/8. Current WP3 D0 is mapped separately. Planned source mappings must become current sources when the implementing WPs land (WP9 owns that refresh). D1 proposal process witnesses are current; complete trial/sink/recall product integration remains pending; current audit/publication fixtures, pure shared rendering, read-only drift/temp-leak diagnostics and graph/identity API/process witnesses are listed above; the current models prove bounded abstract contracts only. Protocol/store/fork and headless smoke witness the existing substrate, not dream conformance. EntryId hashing, validation of bytes/unknown enums, union identity/digest collision rejection, fairness eligibility/quota, actual trial thresholds and budget ranking, atomic no-replace/fsync/link syscalls, committed RecordPins, MCP custody, actual prompt roles, native loader reachability/forgetting and filesystem timing remain implementation-only.

Floating menus (src/frontends/gui/menu.rs) to lab harness-spec.md: "/" menu rows/anchor/8-row window and Enter or click runs the command; header profile switcher (chip, ACP agents then models by provider, filter keys, Esc before interrupt, rows switch through the same Bridge::switch_profile path as /profile NAME; switcher-safe ProfileInfo: key source kind and env presence, agent env count, never a key, a key env value or an agent env value): tests/gui_rich.rs and scripts/parity-web.sh MENU=profiles|slash. contracts.name: HarnessDreamLifecycle
contracts.title: Per-harness dream trial pins, entry-global terminal fences, crash and revival
contracts.assumptions: WP6 D1 maps only its validated Pending/Proposed appends to Propose in the existing lifecycle. Actual bounded prompt/strict JSON/NFC/pin/scope/deny/Usage/source-byte and private-Store/provider/CLI witnesses are tests/dream_pipeline.rs; no later lifecycle, trust authority or semantic audit success is inferred. Resolver's private immutable record memoization index uses safe hashbrown HashTable with production RandomState and existing owned pins; get/insert/clear semantics and one-owner policy invalidation are unchanged. Actual src/dream/resolve.rs unit tests and tests/dream_identity.rs cover complete-pin collision/resize/duplicate/clear behavior, cache hits versus retryable read failures and authorization/revocation transitions, with canonical observable bytes independent of cache seeds. This index is abstracted; finite models do not prove hashbrown/allocator/Hasher memory safety or hash quality, allocations or performance. Refined finite models against dream-log sections 8 and 12; exact native/Java graphs and verdicts are compared, not arbitrary Rust refinement. Current WP4 entry/pin/projection/graph and read-only audit APIs have real private-Git/CLI byte-identity, nofollow/CRLF, read-only and named P1-P9 rejection witnesses. trust.rs implements exact V and external-policy T plus approved artifact validation: dream_trust.rs uses disposable OpenPGP and KB keys, signed private Git roots/gates/tasks, K2, root mismatch, revocation ancestry, policy permissions and executable/capability/gate negatives. receipt.rs implements E and canonical retained R1-R4 with unsynced/unowned/digest/clobber/ABA/conflict/outcome controls and constructive seal.rs custody. E is a trace abstraction of DreamSink, not evidence of effect completeness. The checked typed carrier and operative constructive-seal decision are integrated. receipt.rs/seal.rs implement R1-R4, a constructive per-invocation token, outer publication sealing observation, source/cut/selection/render/adoption checks and explicit fail/unproven distinctions. Complete isolated trusted publication/run/idempotent/stale-exposure fixtures and actual CLI/process witnesses run in dream_audit_broken and dream_seal. No P2/P4 success is inferred from current artifacts or child rows alone. Missing live artifact/scope/receipt proof remains unproven. Actual approved producer completeness, owned-child constraints, gate witness-to-executable bindings, cryptography and syscall bytes remain implementation assumptions/witnesses, never consequences of quotient membership. Cryptography, canonical bytes, signed-root authority and external process effects are implementation-only, not proven by the quotient. contracts.name: HarnessDreamD0
contracts.title: D0 fingerprint claim ownership, atomic pin-set union and detached caller
contracts.assumptions: Two workers, two fingerprint shards, two opaque pins; worker A targets shard0 and B chooses shard0/1 by symmetry. At most one crash and one explicit duplicate replay. Nonvacuity covers independent shard acquisition, busy skip/returned caller while another worker owns, union/duplicate and crashes before/after publish. Lost-union control replaces the union with its own pin; blocking-claim control enters a reachable owned-shard wait and prevents caller return while IO stalls.
